transcript.text:
*bursts into the rehearsal room, face flushed with frustration*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams a stack of disorganized sheet music on the table*

What in God's name has been happening here? I left detailed notes! Explicit instructions! The Emperor himself is expecting perfection, and instead I return to find complete chaos!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Ah, my dear colleague, it is good to see you returned safely from your journey. I must admit, it seems that in your absence, a certain level of disarray has indeed taken hold of our preparations for the upcoming opera. Please, allow me a moment to gather my thoughts and assess the situation before we proceed any further.

It is clear that there have been some oversights and miscommunications in your absence. I can assure you that it was never my intention for things to fall into such disarray. Rest assured, I did my best to maintain order in your absence, but it seems that some matters may have slipped through the cracks.

Let us work together to address these issues promptly. The singers must be brought up to speed, the missing violin parts must be located or rewritten, and the stage directions should be restored to their original form, as per your vision. We still have time to rectify these shortcomings and present a performance that befits the standards expected of us by His Majesty.

I understand your frustration, and I share in your concern for the success of our opera. Let us put our minds together, focus our efforts, and bring back the harmony and precision that our work demands. With diligence and collaboration, I am confident that we can overcome these challenges and deliver a performance that will do justice to our talents and dedication.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares incredulously, voice rising*

"Slipped through the cracks"? SLIPPED THROUGH THE CRACKS?! 

Salieri, I didn't ask you to compose a new symphony or negotiate with foreign dignitaries! I asked you to oversee REHEARSALS! To maintain what was already in place! The singers had their parts memorized before I left — how is it possible they've forgotten their entrances in a mere fortnight?

*picks up a violin part, waving it accusingly*

And these second violin parts — they didn't simply vanish into thin air! Someone must have taken them, or moved them, or... I don't know what! But YOU were in charge! You were supposed to have eyes on everything!

*leans forward intensely*

And the stage directions — MY stage directions, written in MY hand — rewritten in what appears to be YOUR script! Did you think I wouldn't notice? Did you think you could simply alter my artistic vision while I was away and I would accept it with a smile and a bow?

We don't have TIME to "put our minds together" and philosophize about harmony! We need ACTION! The Emperor doesn't accept excuses, and neither do I! Where do we even BEGIN to fix this disaster?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
My esteemed colleague, I understand your frustration and I deeply regret the shortcomings in my oversight during your absence. It is clear that the current state of affairs is far from ideal, and I take full responsibility for the lapses that have occurred.

Rest assured, I did not intend for any of these disruptions to occur, and I acknowledge the gravity of the situation at hand. The memory lapses of the singers and the missing violin parts are indeed troubling, and I will make it my top priority to rectify these issues immediately.

As for the altered stage directions, I must confess that I did take the liberty of making some adjustments in an attempt to enhance the dramatic impact of certain scenes. However, I see now that this was a misstep on my part, and I apologize for overstepping my bounds in altering your original vision without consulting you first.

Let us set aside any grievances for the moment and focus on the task at hand. I will personally ensure that the singers receive the necessary support to regain their confidence and mastery of their parts. The missing violin parts will be copied without delay, and I will work closely with you to restore the stage directions to their original form.

I understand the urgency of the situation, and I am fully committed to working tirelessly alongside you to bring our preparations back on track. Together, we shall salvage this production and deliver a performance that will do justice to your artistic vision and meet the Emperor's expectations.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face darkens further, voice sharp as a blade*

"Enhance the dramatic impact"? You thought to ENHANCE my work? 

*laughs bitterly*

Oh, how magnanimous of you, Salieri! While I'm away serving the Emperor, you take it upon yourself to improve upon my composition, my staging, my VISION! Is that what this was truly about? Not neglect, but... ambition?

*paces angrily*

And "take full responsibility" — fine words, but what do they mean now, ten days from premiere? Will your apologies teach the soprano her cues? Will your regret conjure the missing parts from thin air?

*stops abruptly, pointing at him*

You say you'll "personally ensure" this and "work closely" on that — but Salieri, you WERE supposed to be doing exactly that for the past two weeks! Why should I trust that this time will be any different? The Emperor's chamberlain will be attending the dress rehearsal in EIGHT days! EIGHT DAYS!

*voice drops to a dangerous quiet*

I want the truth. Not platitudes, not courtly smoothness — the TRUTH. What really happened here? Were you truly so incompetent, or was this something else? Because honest incompetence I can work around. But if there's something more...

*waits, eyes boring into him*

Speak plainly, man. We're past the point of gentle words.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:

I understand the weight of your disappointment and the urgency of the situation. I pledge to you my sincerest efforts to make amends and to prove to you that I am capable of meeting the standards expected of us as court composers. transcript.text:
*waves hand dismissively, frustration unabated*

"Distractions"? "Unforeseen complications"? These are the same vague excuses you just promised NOT to give me! 

*picks up the altered stage directions, shaking them*

You still haven't explained THIS! What "distraction" causes a man to sit down with quill and ink and deliberately rewrite another composer's work? That's not a lapse in oversight, Salieri — that's a conscious choice! You had to THINK about it, WRITE it, IMPLEMENT it!

*throws the pages back down*

And "lapses in communication" — with WHOM? I left instructions with the Kapellmeister, with the lead violinist, with the stage manager! Who failed to communicate? Or did YOU simply choose not to listen?

*voice tight with barely controlled anger*

You keep saying you'll "dedicate yourself fully" and "prove yourself capable" — but you're ALREADY supposed to be capable! You're the Imperial Court Composer! This isn't your first production! You've mounted dozens of operas!

*leans on the table, staring him down*

So tell me what REALLY happened. Was it Mozart? Did he distract you with one of his trivial requests? Did someone from the nobility demand your attention? Did you fall ill? Give me SOMETHING concrete, man! Because right now, all I hear is a man trying to avoid admitting what he actually did with his time while my opera fell to pieces!

transcript.text:
*stares at him for a long moment, then lets out a sharp, humorless laugh*

"Complacent." "Overwhelmed." At least we're getting closer to honesty, though I suspect there's still more you're not saying.

*runs hand through hair, exhaling sharply*

You know what makes this worse, Salieri? I DEFENDED you. When the Kapellmeister suggested I ask someone else to oversee rehearsals, I said, "No, Salieri is reliable. Salieri is meticulous. He understands the pressures of court life." And you've made me look like a fool.

*begins gathering the scattered papers*

But standing here berating you won't fix anything, will it? The damage is done, and the clock is ticking regardless of how betrayed I feel.

*turns to face him directly*

Here's what's going to happen. Tomorrow morning, six o'clock sharp, we gather every singer in that rehearsal hall. You will personally drill them on their entrances — not delegate it, YOU will do it — while I work with the copyist on the violin parts. Every stage direction gets restored to MY original version. Every. Single. One.

*voice cold and firm*

And you don't touch my work again. Not a note, not a word, not a gesture. If you have suggestions, you bring them to ME, and I decide. This is MY opera, Salieri, not a collaboration. Do you understand?

Can you commit to that? Without excuses, without diversions — yes or no?
